case_title: Haresh Mohandas Rajput v. State of Maharashtra
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (lived in close vicinity for a long time and was well acquainted with the victim and her family)
weapon: Rope (alleged; the Trial Court disbelieved that it was the rope used, and the High Court's finding on it was given little weight)
evidence_type: Circumstantial; medical (post-mortem); recovery of body and blood-stained articles; chemical analysis; testimony of child witness; police and witness evidence of information given at police station
confession: Alleged extra-judicial confession to mother and son Khushal (PW.10). Not relied on: Khushal was declared hostile and the mother was not examined, so the Court held the confession was not proved.
aggravating_circumstances: Rape and strangulation of a 10-year-old girl; sexual assault injuries; body found concealed under the cot; blood on bed-sheet and floor
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 and s.376; life imprisonment under s.302 and 10 years under s.376, sentences to run concurrently
high_court_outcome: Conviction confirmed; State's appeal for enhancement allowed and sentence altered from life imprisonment to death
neutral_facts: On a late afternoon in October 1999, the victim, a ten-year-old girl, was playing on a road near the accused's house with her brother and sister. When she was found missing, her brother searched for her without success. Her mother, who had been away at work, returned and also searched, but the victim could not be traced. The brother later said a friend had told him the victim was in the accused's house. He went to the rear of the house and said he saw the victim lying in a room, and when he asked the accused about her, the accused denied she was there. Another person entered from the back of the house but did not see her. On that day the accused's mother and son had gone out, leaving the accused alone in the house. The accused's son later went to the police and reported that the accused had killed the girl and that her body lay under a cot in the house. Police went to the house with the victim's father and recovered the body from under the cot, while the accused was sitting outside. Blood was found on a bed-sheet, on the cot and on the floor beneath it, and the clothing and cloth pieces were found to contain human blood. The post-mortem found injuries consistent with sexual assault, ligature marks on the neck and death by strangulation. The accused could not explain how the body came to be in his house and said he had gone to a liquor shop and left the house open.
physical_harm: Death by strangulation with ligature marks around the neck of a 10-year-old girl; genital injuries consistent with sexual assault, including torn hymen; multiple facial and limb contusions and abrasions, all ante-mortem
premeditation_planning: Not found. The Court did not find premeditation or planning; it noted only an attempt to conceal the body under the cot.
key_evidence_accepted: Recovery of body from under cot in the accused's house; blood on bed-sheet and floor (spot panchnama); chemical report showing human blood on clothing and cloth pieces; post-mortem evidence of sexual assault and strangulation; police-station information given by the accused's son (PW.10); accused's admission in s.313 examination that he was sitting outside and that the body was recovered; the victim's disappearance from play and the accused's presence at the house.
witness_credibility: Mother (PW.1), father (PW.2), Deepak Jawahar Agarwal (PW.8) and Head Constable G.R. More (PW.4) were found credible and uncontradicted on cross-examination. Khushal (PW.10) was declared hostile and his evidence was assessed with caution. The child witness Nitesh (PW.3) was accepted on the disappearance and presence of the accused; his account of seeing the victim in the house was rejected by the Trial Court and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere. The doctor's post-mortem evidence was not challenged.
post_offence_conduct: Found sitting outside his house when police arrived; gave an explanation of going to a liquor shop and leaving the house open, which the courts found false and unsubstantiated
trial_duration: offence: 24.10.1999; trial judgment: 19.9.2001; High Court: 11.01.2008; Supreme Court: 20.09.2011
legal_representation: Appellant: D.N. Goburdhan, Prabal Bagchi, Karitka Sharma, Balendu Shekhar. State: Arun R. Pednekar, Sanjay Kharde, Aisha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: FIR lodged; body recovered and panchnama prepared; accused arrested; chargesheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Police entered the house before the panchnama was prepared, which the Trial Court held weakened the rope recovery
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 and s.376 IPC, life imprisonment and 10 years concurrent. High Court: conviction upheld; death sentence substituted on State's appeal. Supreme Court: conviction affirmed; death sentence set aside and life imprisonment restored.
prosecution_argument: Dead body recovered from accused's house; medical evidence showed strangulation after sexual assault; any inconsistencies in witness statements were trivial; concurrent findings of the courts below should not be disturbed
defence_argument: No evidence connects the accused to the crime; circumstantial evidence did not exclude hypotheses of innocence; material inconsistencies in witness statements; no sufficient evidence for conviction; death sentence not justified on any ground
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence test: circumstances must be fully established, conclusive, consistent only with guilt, exclude every other hypothesis, and form a chain so complete that the accused's guilt is the only probable inference. Rarest of rare test for death sentence: aggravating circumstances must exist and mitigating circumstances must be absent, with reference to the Bachan Singh and Machhi Singh framework.
precedent_relied_upon: Krishnan v. State (2008) 15 SCC 430; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1984 SC 1622; Paramjeet Singh @ Pamma v. State of Uttarakhand AIR 2011 SC 200; Wakkar v. State of UP (2011) 3 SCC 306; Mohd. Mannan v. State of Bihar (2011) 5 SCC 317; Inspector of Police v. John David (2011) 5 SCC 509; SK Yusuf v. State of West Bengal AIR 2011 SC 2283; Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1980 SC 898 and Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1983 SC 957 (death sentence guidelines); C. Muniappan AIR 2010 SC 3718; Rabindra Kumar Pal (2011) 2 SCC 490; Surendra Koli (2011) 4 SCC 80; Sudam @ Rahul Kaniram Jadhav (2011) 7 SCC 125
sentencing_rationale: The case did not fall within the rarest of rare category, so the death sentence awarded by the High Court was set aside and life imprisonment restored
judicial_aggravating_factors: Court referred to the sexual assault and strangulation and the attempt to conceal the body; it nonetheless held the case did not fall within the rarest of rare category
